choice.div: The column(s) that uniquely identify each row in a table.
Any column that can be sorted.
The first column of the table.

div.p: A primary key is the unique, non-null identifier for a row; other tables point at it with a foreign key.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A learner can enrol in many courses, and a course has many learners. This is modelled as:

choice.div: A many-to-many relationship, via a join table holding both keys.
A single foreign key on the learners table.
A column listing every course in the learners row.

div.p: Many-to-many always needs a third table whose rows are the pairings — that is what the enrolment table is.

choiceresponse.p: Which are reasons to normalise? Select all that apply.

choice.div: To avoid repeating the same fact in many rows.
To stop an update needing to be made in several places.
To make every query faster in every case.
To prevent losing unrelated information when deleting a row.

div.p: Normalisation removes the insert/update/delete anomalies by storing each fact once. It is not automatically faster — sometimes it trades joins for consistency.
